# Seed proposal

<!-- slot-head:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->
<div class="gp-chips"><span class="gp-chip">Seed-based · 5 methods</span><code class="gp-chip">--set proposal=</code><span class="gp-chip">24 options</span></div>
<!-- slot-head:end -->

The seed proposal picks the points of the scene at which grasps are predicted, the same number
in every frame. It is the only stage that decides where the rest of the model looks.

## Use it

<!-- method-options:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->

=== "GraspNet-baseline"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set proposal=graspness-sfps -o graspnet-baseline_graspness-sfps.yaml
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e --list proposal
    ```

=== "GSNet"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set proposal=graspness-sfps -o gsnet_graspness-sfps.yaml
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list proposal
    ```

=== "Scale-Balanced-Grasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set proposal=graspness-sfps -o scale-balanced-grasp_graspness-sfps.yaml
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --list proposal
    ```

=== "EconomicGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set proposal=graspness-sfps -o economicgrasp_graspness-sfps.yaml
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list proposal
    ```

=== "FineGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set proposal=graspness-sfps -o finegrasp_graspness-sfps.yaml
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list proposal
    ```

The first command writes a checked config; the second lists every option of the slot under that method, with what was measured. Then `grasppanda probe <file>` tries the config on real frames and `grasppanda train <file>` trains it ([Swap a component](../get_started/swap.md)). Each method page lists the same: [GraspNet-baseline](../methods/graspnet_baseline.md#proposal) · [GSNet](../methods/gsnet.md#proposal) · [Scale-Balanced-Grasp](../methods/scale_balanced_grasp.md#proposal) · [EconomicGrasp](../methods/economicgrasp.md#proposal) · [FineGrasp](../methods/finegrasp.md#proposal).

## Choosing

- **Start from the method's own proposal**, marked *own* in the table, and change one thing.
- **Spread or rank.** `graspness-sfps` and `graspness-fps-topk` keep the seeds spread over the
  scene; `graspness-topk` takes the best-scored points wherever they are.
- **No score at all.** The `dense-*` options sample among all scene points; they predict
  nothing and need no labels of their own.
- **A score needs its labels.** The scoring options read point-wise graspness labels:
  `grasppanda prepare graspnet1b --graspness --camera <camera> --config <config>` builds them
  once.
- **Seeds feed the grouper.** A grouper that crops among the seeds sees their density, so
  check it again after a change here.

## Details

??? note "How a proposal is built: five choices"

    Every published proposal is the same five choices, and each is an option here.

    | Choice | What it decides | Where it is set |
    |---|---|---|
    | scorer | what is predicted per scene point (objectness, graspness, nothing) | the proposal class |
    | selecting score | which score cuts and ranks | `select_by` |
    | candidate rule | threshold, product threshold or rank cut | `graspness_threshold`, `objectness_threshold`, `top_fraction` |
    | sampler | which candidates become seeds | `sampler: {type: ...}`, a component of its own |
    | too few points | what a frame with fewer candidates than seeds gets | `too_few` |

    The four proposal classes:

    | Class | Scorer | Requires | Predicts |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `GraspnessFPS` | objectness + graspness | dense features | graspness, objectness; selection and sampler fixed, with the two quirks of the reference sampling kernel |
    | `ScoredSeeds` | objectness + graspness (the same targets and losses) | dense features | graspness, objectness; selecting score, candidate rule, sampler and padding are options |
    | `SubsampledSeeds` | none | a sub-sampling encoder | nothing; the encoder's subsample is the seed set |
    | `SampledSeeds` | none | dense features | nothing; a sampler picks among all scene points |

??? note "Input and output"

    `proposal(feats, observation) -> (SeedSet, scores)` and
    `proposal.loss(scores, supervision) -> dict`.

    | | Type | Content |
    |---|---|---|
    | in | `PointFeatures` | `(N, C)` features of the encoder, bound to the points of the whole batch (frames told apart by `points.batch_offsets`); `C` is injected (`in_channels`). |
    | in | `Observation` | `points`: the scene, `(N, 3)` in metres, camera frame. |
    | out | `SeedSet` | `B × num_seeds` seeds, each a scene point (`parent_index`); their features, still attached to the encoder's graph; named per-seed scores (`graspness`, `objectness`), detached; `valid`, false for padding; `source`, how they were chosen. |
    | out | scores | what the proposal's own `loss` needs (`PointScores` for a scoring proposal, `None` otherwise). |

    What the neighbours require:

    - **Every frame yields exactly `num_seeds` seeds**, so later stages work on dense
      `(B, M, …)` tensors. Padding is marked `valid = False` and never becomes a grasp; the
      share of real seeds is logged as `metric/real_seeds`.
    - **Seeds are scene points.** Assigners match labels through `parent_index`; no option
      invents positions.
    - **Seeds are chosen from the predictions in training too**, so a sampler changes which
      examples the view stage and the head learn from, from the first iteration.

    The contract attributes, compared by `grasppanda compose` before anything is built:

    | Attribute | Values | Rule |
    |---|---|---|
    | `requires` | `dense`, `subsampled`, `any` | must equal the encoder's `output`; compose inserts the adapter (`FeaturePropagation` or `FurthestPointSubsample`) and says so. |
    | `seed_scores` | the scores it predicts | one owner per score. Next to `ObjectnessViewStage`, which predicts objectness too, compose makes a scoring proposal select by graspness only and says so; one that selects by objectness is refused. |
    | `sampler_inputs` against the sampler's `needs` | `scores`, `feats` | a sampler that reads scores is refused inside a proposal that predicts none. |

??? note "Samplers: `model.proposal.sampler`"

    A sampler has no parameters, so there are no weights to load. `grasppanda components --slot
    samplers` lists them.

    | Sampler | What it is | Paper | Code | Reads | Extra |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | `FPS` | furthest point sampling on coordinates; start `first` or `random` | PointNet++, NeurIPS 2017 | `grasppanda.ops.furthest_point_sample` | coordinates | none |
    | `FeatureFPS` | furthest point sampling in feature space (F-FPS) | [3DSSD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10187), CVPR 2020 | written from the definition; distances as in [3DSSD@8bc7605](https://github.com/dvlab-research/3DSSD/blob/8bc7605/lib/utils/layers_util.py#L84-L111) (MIT) | features | none |
    | `FusionFPS` | part of the seeds by F-FPS, the rest by coordinates (FS) | 3DSSD, CVPR 2020 | as above | features | none |
    | `ScoreWeightedFPS` | semantics-guided FPS (S-FPS): maximise score^γ × distance | [SASA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.01976), AAAI 2022 | written from the definition; kernel read in [SASA@cd79f60](https://github.com/blakechen97/SASA/blob/cd79f60/pcdet/ops/pointnet2/pointnet2_batch/src/sampling_gpu.cu#L414-L463) (Apache-2.0) | scores | none |
    | `TopK` | the best-scored points, no spread | [IA-SSD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11139), CVPR 2022; the last step of [GraNet](https://github.com/wang-h-w/GraNet/tree/d9992e1), IROS 2023 | `torch.sort` | scores | none |
    | `RandomSampler` | uniform, without replacement, own seeded generator | the sampling ablation of GSNet (ICCV 2021); RandLA-Net (CVPR 2020) | `torch.randperm` | coordinates | none |
    | `VoxelGridSampler` | one point per occupied voxel (the best-scored one when scores exist) | regular subsampling as in [KPConv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.08889), ICCV 2019 | `grasppanda.ops.voxelize` | coordinates | none |
    | `FPSThenTopK` | FPS for coverage, then the best-scored of the rest | the selection rule of [Contact-GraspNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14127), ICRA 2021 | written from the description (its code is under a non-commercial licence and was not copied) | scores | none |
    | `ScoreNMS` | best score first, no two seeds closer than a radius | Algorithm 1 of [S4G](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.14218), CoRL 2019 | written from the paper (the repository has no licence file) | scores | none |
    | `FpsampleFPS` | CPU furthest point sampling, bucket-based QuickFPS and four other methods | QuickFPS (IEEE TCAD 2023, as the library cites it) | bridge to [`fpsample`](https://github.com/leonardodalinky/fpsample) (MIT) | coordinates | `fpsample` |
    | `TorchClusterFPS` | the furthest point sampling kernel of PyTorch Geometric | PointNet++, NeurIPS 2017 | bridge to [`torch_cluster.fps`](https://github.com/rusty1s/pytorch_cluster) (MIT) | coordinates | `torch-cluster` |

??? note "The settings that matter"

    Any sampler goes inside either proposal that has one:

    ```yaml
    model:
      proposal:
        type: ScoredSeeds
        num_seeds: 1024
        select_by: graspness_and_objectness   # graspness | objectness | product
        graspness_threshold: 0.1
        objectness_threshold: 0.5
        top_fraction: null                    # e.g. 0.1: a rank cut instead of the thresholds
        too_few: pad                          # best_rest: fill with the best other points
        sampler: {type: ScoreWeightedFPS, gamma: 1.0}
    ```

    | Setting | How to choose |
    |---|---|
    | `select_by` | `graspness_and_objectness` is GSNet's rule. `graspness` drops the objectness test (objectness is still trained). `objectness` makes every predicted object point a candidate. `product` cuts `P(object) × graspness`, MultiGraspNet's rule ([arXiv 2602.06504](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06504)). |
    | `graspness_threshold` | belongs to the label definition: 0.1 for graspness normalised to [0, 1] per frame (GSNet) or per instance (FineGrasp). Change the label, change the threshold. |
    | `top_fraction` | a rank cut: the best share of each frame's points, whatever their values ([DexGraspNet 2.0](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.23004) keeps the top 1 % before FPS). With 15 000 points a frame it must be at least 0.07 to leave 1024 candidates; the preset uses 0.1. |
    | `too_few` | `pad`: a frame without candidates has no real seed and trains the proposal only, as in the first iterations of every run. `best_rest`: such a frame gets the best-scored other points as real seeds. |
    | `sampler.gamma` (`ScoreWeightedFPS`) | 0 is FPS started at the best point, 1 is SASA's reference, large values approach top-k. `distance: squared` is the released kernel, `euclidean` the paper's formula. |
    | `sampler.metric`, `sampler.coord_weight` (`FeatureFPS`, `FusionFPS`) | `concat` is the released 3DSSD code, `sum` is Eq. 1 of the paper. With 512 feature channels the coordinates hardly count; raise `coord_weight` or set `normalize: true` when the seeds cluster. |
    | `sampler.voxel_size`, `sampler.min_distance` | decide how many real seeds a scene yields: read `metric/real_seeds` from a probe and adapt. |
    | `sampler.seed` | an integer makes two evaluations pick the same seeds. |

    A checkpoint of GSNet, EconomicGrasp or FineGrasp loads strictly into a model whose
    proposal is `ScoredSeeds` (the scorer is the same layer), so a sampler can also be swapped
    at test time on a trained model. That is a different experiment from training with it;
    say in the config which one it is.

??? warning "Pitfalls met while building this"

    - **`fpsample`'s bucket methods do not begin at `start_idx`.** `vanilla` returns exactly the
      indices of `grasppanda.ops.furthest_point_sample`; `bucket` spreads as well but returns
      another seed set; the `npdu` methods assume points in scan order and spread worse than
      random sampling on a shuffled cloud. Use `method: vanilla` to match the reference.
    - **The CPU bridges are not faster here.** They are for CPU-only inference and for the same
      kernel as another code base.
    - **`torch_cluster.fps` takes a ratio, not a count,** and starts at a random point. The
      bridge converts the count, trims the result and sets `random_start: false`.
    - **Three distances are called F-FPS.** The 3DSSD paper, its released code and SASA's code
      differ; `metric` and `coord_weight` name the convention.
    - **S-FPS: paper and kernel differ by a factor of two in γ.** The kernel multiplies the
      *squared* distance by `score^γ`; `distance` names the convention.
    - **3DSSD's fusion sampling returns twice the points.** A proposal has a fixed seed count,
      so `FusionFPS` splits it between the two kinds (`feature_fraction`).
    - **A score above 1 must not be clamped.** Predicted graspness is not bounded by 1;
      clamping tied every value above 1 and top-k fell back to the first k points. The
      selecting score is now only kept non-negative.
    - **Feature-space sampling over the whole scene is the most expensive option here.** Picks
      stay on the device and a feature distance is one matrix-vector product per pick.

??? note "Not wrapped"

    | Candidate | Why not |
    |---|---|
    | Object-balanced seeds (a quota per instance), as in Scale-Balanced-Grasp and DexGraspNet 2.0 | needs an instance mask at test time, which no dataset or transform fills yet; the sampler side would be a small wrapper. |
    | GraNet's cascaded selection ([GraNet@d9992e1](https://github.com/wang-h-w/GraNet/tree/d9992e1), MIT) | brings its own graph encoder and a ten-class label no dataset here builds; its last step is `graspness-topk`. |
    | MultiGraspNet's graspness loss | a loss, not a proposal; its candidate rule is `product-fps`. |
    | RandLA-Net, S4G and Contact-GraspNet code | licences (CC BY-NC-SA, none, NVIDIA); the small rules were written from the papers. |
    | PyTorch3D, Open3D and mmcv samplers | need compiled builds; a third and fourth spelling of the same FPS. |
    | Voted seeds (VoteGrasp), mask queries (M2T2), image heat-map centres (HGGD) | they emit virtual seeds or a variable number of regions; the skeleton needs scene points. |
    | A sampler inside the encoders, where 3DSSD, IA-SSD and SASA place theirs | a change to the encoders, not to this slot; the `SAMPLERS` registry is ready for it. |
